Gaze results mapped to the instruction manual — figures and evidence

36 participants (17 experts, 19 non-experts), 360 recordings. Odd recordings = disassembly, even = assembly. Shares are of labelled fixation time, participant means. Every figure is followed by the exact numbers it plots.

Figure 00. The manual as a process

Insight. Assembly reverses disassembly; steps group into five phases; colour (green vs red screwdriver, red vs blue box) carries step identity.

Proof from our data. Seven reverse pairs: D7↔A1, D6↔A3, D4↔A4, D5↔A5, D3↔A6, D2↔A7, D1↔A8. A2 (turn gear to seat) and D8 (sort) have no counterpart.

Source tables: manual_step_catalog.csv

Figure 01. Manual use is a learning curve

Insight. Manual dependence halves about every three recordings; non-experts reach the experts' first-recording level only at recording 8; recordings 9–10 break the curve.

Proof from our data. Non-experts 52.0% → 10.0% over recordings 1–8 (ρ = −0.98), experts 11.5% → 3.3% (ρ = −0.76). Decay per recording −20% (non-experts) and −16% (experts). Recording 8 → 9: 10.0% → 0.5% (20-fold) for non-experts.

Source tables: manual_share_by_task_repetition.csv, chronological_manual_curve.csv, manual_learning_fit.csv

Figure 02. Learning happens within each pair

Insight. Non-experts cut manual use mostly between a disassembly and the assembly that follows it, not between repetitions.

Proof from our data. Non-experts: all 4 within-pair transitions drop 20–41% (median −30%); between-pair transitions change +1%, −6%, −12% (median −6%). Experts: within-pair median −30% at a low base level; between-pair changes are noisy (−48%, +159%, −38%).

Source tables: manual_share_by_task_repetition.csv, manual_change_within_vs_between_pairs.csv

Figure 03. Attention signatures of direction and expertise

Insight. Assembly shifts gaze to the grinder, disassembly to the screwdriver; experts replace manual reading with box and tool gaze.

Proof from our data. Assembly − disassembly: grinder +10.3 / +9.0 pp, screwdriver −9.1 / −6.7 pp (experts / non-experts). Expert − non-expert in disassembly: manual −19.5 pp, box +9.7 pp, screwdriver +9.5 pp, grinder +0.3 pp.

Source tables: attention_share_by_task_expertise.csv, direction_effect.csv, expertise_gap.csv

Figure 04. Experts do, non-experts read

Insight. Experts spend ~70% of labelled gaze on execution in both directions; non-experts 60–63%. Experts' box share is flat; non-experts' rises in assembly.

Proof from our data. Execution share: experts 70.2% / 71.4%, non-experts 60.5% / 63.1% (disassembly / assembly). Box share: experts 24.3% → 24.6%, non-experts 14.6% → 20.0%.

Source tables: attention_budget.csv, attention_share_by_task_expertise.csv

Figure 05. Gaze routes follow the manual's action order

Insight. Unscrew → remove → deposit dominates disassembly; fetch → place → fasten dominates assembly; deposit → read marks disassembly step boundaries.

Proof from our data. T→W→S : S→W→T = 160 : 120 in disassembly and 140 : 215 in assembly. Fetch–fit–fetch (S→W→S) 2.68 per assembly recording vs 1.17 per disassembly recording (2.3×), in 81% of assembly recordings. Deposit → read (W→S→C) in 75 of 180 disassembly recordings (42%) and 30 of 36 participants; not among the top assembly routes.

Source tables: top_routes_by_direction.csv, routes_mapped_to_manual.csv

Figure 06. Timing anchor: the wrench step

Insight. Assembly has a slow front end (A1–A2); tool steps are watched at the target, so the wrench anchors only a third of recordings.

Proof from our data. Median first wrench gaze: D6 132 s (n = 8), A3 180 s (n = 8). Wrench gaze in 61/180 disassembly and 54/180 assembly recordings; 0.3–0.7% of labelled gaze.

Source tables: wrench_intervals_report_excerpt.csv, wrench_anchor_timing_excerpt.csv, attention_share_by_task_expertise.csv

Figure 07. How well can gaze name the step?

Insight. Today's five labels identify the phase well but merge steps inside the screw block; step-aware labels (colours, side handle, armature, hand) separate most steps.

Proof from our data. 5-label windows: D3 0% and A6 1% exact (merge with D2 / A7), A8 0%; wrench steps 90–92%. 10-label means: exact step 48–60% today vs 73–77% step-aware; phase 82–86% vs 95–96%.

Source tables: step_discriminability_model.csv, configs/manual_steps.yaml

Figure 08. Predicting the step from a sequence

Insight. Today's labels pin the phase almost certainly but spread the probability over the steps of the block; colour labels resolve the step.

Proof from our data. A: unscrew block 99.8%, D3 39% vs D2 37%. B: screw block certain, step spread over A4–A7. C: A4 91%.
